favourite.heading: Why Delaware can pull away
bullets: Playing at Delaware is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

Delaware is the better football team by 2.3 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 74% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+2.3 pts).
Stylistically the matchup favours Delaware by 0.9 points: ball control vs front disruption (+0.9 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Coastal Carolina can keep it close
bullets: Conference strength differs and the in-season sample is still thin, worth 0.4 points to Coastal Carolina (-0.4 pts).
The outcome range is 15.3 points wide at one sigma — p10 -16.1 to p90 +27.9 for Delaware, so a projection of +6.9 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 4%.
College ratings are built on twelve-game seasons against wildly uneven schedules; even a clean rating gap carries more estimation error than the number implies.
